description: Library/version evidence for draft-versus-final PQC. Every version rule must cite a source. Libraries without verified version rules always yield 'needs_manual_verification'.

Kyber.note: 'Kyber' is the name of the CRYSTALS-Kyber submission. FIPS 203 standardised it as ML-KEM with changes, so Round-3 Kyber and ML-KEM are not interoperable. The name alone does not prove which version an implementation uses.

Dilithium.note: 'Dilithium' is the name of the CRYSTALS-Dilithium submission. FIPS 204 standardised it as ML-DSA with changes. The name alone does not prove which version an implementation uses.

version_rules.evidence: liboqs 0.10.0 (2024-03-23) added implementations of the Initial Public Draft (IPD) of ML-KEM; the update to final FIPS 203 is recorded in 0.11.0 (2024-09-29).
liboqs 0.11.0 (2024-09-29) release notes state ML-KEM implementations were updated to the final FIPS 203 version.
liboqs 0.10.0 added the Initial Public Draft (IPD) of ML-DSA; the update to final FIPS 204 is recorded in 0.12.0 (2024-12-10).
liboqs 0.12.0 (2024-12-10) release notes state the ML-DSA implementation was updated to the final FIPS 204 version.
liboqs 0.11.0 notes Round-3 Kyber is kept only for interoperability; 0.12.0 states it is the last release to include Kyber and that applications should switch to ML-KEM (FIPS 203).
liboqs 0.12.0 notes NIST Round-3 Dilithium is kept only for interoperability and is planned for removal; ML-DSA implements FIPS 204.

sources.title: liboqs changelog as packaged by openSUSE (mirrors upstream release notes)

libraries.name: liboqs-python (Python wrapper for liboqs)
libraries.manual_note: The wrapper version does not by itself establish which liboqs C library is loaded at runtime, so QuantumGuard does not map wrapper versions to FIPS status. Check the loaded C library version (e.g. oqs.oqs_version()) and compare it with the liboqs rules.

indicator_status.evidence: Go documentation (go1.24.0) states crypto/mlkem implements ML-KEM (formerly known as Kyber) as specified in NIST FIPS 203.
